subject: Intermittent gateway rewrite causing partial reachability — Horizon deployment
messages:
From: Horizon IT <netops@horizonhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: connectivity to on-prem model nodes flapping after gateway change

Hi Evelyn,

We pushed the scheduled edge gateway rewrite at 02:30 UTC this morning (change: consolidated NAT translations and a new outbound rewrite rule to strip a stale CNAME). Since then, our app stack intermittently loses connectivity to the Redwood inference edge (specific to the on-prem model serving cluster in our colo). Connectivity drops last ~30–90s, then recovers. The issue affects only certain front-end pods — others talk fine.

Attached are a traceroute and a brief pcap sample captured during a hit window. We also grabbed the route table snapshot from our edge box.

High-level symptoms:
- TCP connections SYNs reach your edge but the TCP handshake stalls (SYN, SYN-ACK not completed) for affected flows.
- Traces show differing next-hops in the middle of the path (sometimes a rewrite hop appears).
- No obvious firewall deny logs on our side.

Can you confirm whether the new rewrite could be causing asymmetric routing or an unexpected SNAT that would break connection tracking? We're holding a customer-facing incident call at 13:00 PT if helpful.

Thanks,
Carlos
Horizon Health — NetOps

[Attachments: horizon_traceroute_0908.txt (text), horizon_capture_0908.pcap (pcap), route-table-snap.png (png)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Horizon IT <netops@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: connectivity to on-prem model nodes flapping after gateway change

Carlos — thanks for the quick data. Looping in Marissa (networking lead) and Karthik (on-prem infra) to triage; Connor from incident rotation will join the 13:00 PT call.

Initial asks:
- Can you share an example affected flow 5-tuple (src ip:port -> dst ip:port) and the timestamp when it failed? That helps correlate conntrack and NAT table holes.
- Please confirm whether the rewrite was targeted at a specific backend pool or applied globally.
- If safe, keep one affected VM in debug mode (tcpdump + netstat -tn) so we can capture conntrack state when it drops.

Quick note from our side: the rewrite you mentioned matches a recent change to allow host-header based rewrites; if the rewrite incorrectly strips/rewrites source IPs an unexpected SNAT could be introduced which would indeed break symmetric return path assumptions.

Evelyn
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Horizon IT <netops@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: connectivity to on-prem model nodes flapping after gateway change

Thanks Carlos — I pulled the traceroute and the route table image. A few early observations:

- The traceroute shows a rewrite (TTL-preserving probe shows an extra hop that rewrites the source), which is suspicious for a middlebox performing NAT masquerade on a subset of flows.
- route-table-snap.png indicates two overlapping egress policies: one global rewrite policy and one client-specific path. If the rewrite engine evaluates policies out-of-order, some sessions could be translated while others bypass translation — that explains the intermittent nature.

Immediate triage plan:
1) Karthik, can you export the conntrack/NAT table for the affected edge box at the timestamps Carlos provided? Look for entries where src IPs are SNATed to the edge's public IP.
2) Carlos — please run a short tcpdump with the exact 5-tuple Evelyn requested when you see a failure and attach as horizon_capture_snip.pcap.
3) Connor — on the 13:00 call, be prepared to flip the rewrite policy to opt-in (rather than global) as a short-lived rollback. That should remove the asymmetric path if the rewrite is the cause.

Also, what's the MTU between Horizon's edge and our colo? Fragmentation could exacerbate connection stalls, especially for TLS handshakes that push larger MSS values.

Marissa
Sr. Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@horizonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: connectivity to on-prem model nodes flapping after gateway change

Marissa — thanks, attaching a focused pcap and the 5-tuple examples. Observations from our capture:
- We see SYN -> SYN-ACK from your edge, but occasionally the SYN-ACK is sourced from an IP that doesn’t match the expected next-hop (rewritten IP in 10.254.x.x space).
- MTU between our edge and colo shows PMTU at 1452 on the path during tests; our MSS clamp is 1400 to be safe.

Attached: horizon_capture_snip.pcap (90s) and examples.txt with 5-tuples. We can keep a host in capture for the 13:00 window.

Carlos

[Attachments: horizon_capture_snip.pcap (pcap), examples.txt (text)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Horizon IT <netops@horizonhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T15:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: connectivity to on-prem model nodes flapping after gateway change

Update after correlating Horizon captures with our edge logs (notes from the 13:00 PT incident call):

Root cause hypothesis: an evaluation-order bug in the new rewrite engine caused a narrow set of flows (matching a host-header + path prefix) to be routed through an internal rewrite proxy that performed an additional SNAT to a link-local address for header normalization. The proxy failed to preserve the original 5-tuple for return traffic, causing conntrack mismatches and transient handshake stalls. Two compounding factors:
1) The policy applied globally for a 10-minute deployment window during the rollout, hitting a subset of front-end pods.
2) A PMTU discrepancy (1452 vs expected 1500) means some reassembled packets were larger and more sensitive to translation timing, increasing the chance of missed handshake completion.

Remediation taken:
- Rolled back the rewrite to opt-in policy at 13:05 PT (immediate reduction in reported incidents).
- Updated rewrite engine to avoid SNAT on normal TCP flows; added a fast-path that preserves source IP/port for established handshakes. Patch request created: INF-4021.
- Added a temporary conntrack metric alert to surface sudden SNAT ratio changes.

Follow-ups / action items:
- We recommend Horizon keep MSS clamp at 1400 for the next 48 hours while we monitor.
- Connor will follow up with a small postmortem (attach our pcap correlation and a short timeline).
- Marissa/Karthik to schedule a code fix verification and a canary rollout plan that exercises host-header rewrites without global exposure.

Thanks everyone for the quick collaboration — feel free to re-open if you see new occurrences.

Karthik
On-Prem Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

[Attachments referenced: horizon_netdiag_20261220.tar.gz, route-table-snap.png]
